haiku-low.q1: It is held for 10 minutes. If the order does not claim it in time, the hold expires.
haiku-low.q2: Before. Stock is reserved first, then the customer is charged. If any line is short, nothing is reserved, no payment is requested, and the order is cancelled.
haiku-low.q3: The order id is sent as the idempotency key, so the provider treats a repeated request with the same key as the same charge.
haiku-low.q4: If stock is still free, it is reserved and claimed again and the order is confirmed. If any line is sold, money is refunded in full automatically, the order is cancelled as out of stock, and the customer is emailed.
haiku-low.q5: Only after the order is confirmed, when the Cart service receives the order-confirmed event. If checkout fails for any reason, the cart stays exactly as it was.
haiku-low.q6: NOT STATED. The Order service creates the pending order and asks Inventory and Payment for steps, but the document does not name a driver or a per-checkout progress record.
haiku-low.q7: The provider sends a webhook to the Payment service, which stores it as handled and processes it. The Order service then acts on the result.
haiku-low.q8: Payment checks its database for whether it already handled the webhook. A repeat is ignored. How a repeat is recognised is not decided; the provider's event id is one option.
haiku-low.q9: Payment records the decline. The Order service marks the order failed, and the Inventory service releases the hold so the stock goes back on sale. The cart is unchanged.
haiku-low.q10: Inventory checks whether stock is still free for every line. If yes, it reserves and claims it and the order is confirmed. If any line is gone, the payment is refunded.
haiku-low.q11: Payment records the failed refund and retries it, and it is raised to a person. Refunds are never dropped silently. The retry limit and alerting are not set.
haiku-low.q12: The order-confirmed event, published by the Order service after confirmation, causes the Cart service to empty the cart. How a lost or late event is recovered is not decided.

sonnet.q1: Held for 10 minutes. If the order does not claim it, the hold expires (the stock is then free and may be sold to someone else).
sonnet.q2: Stock is reserved before the charge. If any line is short, nothing is reserved (all or nothing), no payment is requested, the order is cancelled, the customer is told which items are short, and the cart is unchanged.
sonnet.q3: The idempotency key (the order id) is sent with every charge; the provider treats a repeat with the same key as the same charge, so at most one charge.
sonnet.q4: Payment automatically refunds the full amount, and the Order service cancels the order as out of stock and emails the customer. No partial order is shipped.
sonnet.q5: The cart is emptied only after the order is confirmed (on the order-confirmed event). If checkout fails for any reason, the cart stays exactly as it was.
sonnet.q6: NOT STATED as a single coordinator. The document says the Order service asks the others over HTTP and the services react via events, but it names no orchestrator and no single record of checkout progress (only the order's status in the Order service's database, with status names not fixed).
sonnet.q7: The provider sends a webhook to us, handled by the Payment service; the Order service then marks the order failed or confirmed. The document does not say exactly how Payment's result is passed to Order (HTTP or event is not specified).
sonnet.q8: Payment checks its database for whether it already handled the webhook; a repeat is ignored and a new one is stored as handled, then processed. How a repeat is recognised (e.g. provider event id) is not decided.
sonnet.q9: The Inventory service releases the hold so the stock goes back on sale; it is triggered by the declined outcome (webhook) after Payment records the decline and the Order service marks the order failed. The exact trigger mechanism between services is not specified.
sonnet.q10: Inventory checks whether stock is still free for every line. If yes, it reserves and claims it and the order is confirmed (money kept). If any line is gone, Payment refunds in full and the order is cancelled as out of stock.
sonnet.q11: Payment records the failed refund and retries it, and it is raised to a person; it is never silently dropped. It is tracked as a recorded failed refund by Payment (presumably in its database; retry limit and alerting not set).
sonnet.q12: The Order service publishing the order-confirmed event on the message broker causes it; the Cart service receives the event and empties the cart.
